stem: Which seizure type is an absolute requirement for the diagnosis of Juvenile Myoclonic Epilepsy (JME)?
explanation: Myoclonic jerks, typically occurring upon awakening, are the hallmark feature and required for a JME diagnosis.
rationale: The name of the syndrome itself provides a clue to the mandatory seizure manifestation.

optionExplanations.A: Absence seizures occur in only a minority of JME patients and are not necessary for the diagnosis.
optionExplanations.B: While the vast majority of patients will have these, the diagnosis specifically hinges on a different, more characteristic seizure type.
optionExplanations.C: Myoclonic jerks, typically occurring upon awakening, are the hallmark feature and required for a JME diagnosis.
optionExplanations.D: JME is an idiopathic generalized epilepsy; focal seizures would suggest a different classification.
